lede: Nvidia dropped 14% on a report of an SEC look at its accounting, and the 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 4.99%.

items.title: Nvidia falls 14% after report of SEC look at its accounting
facts: Nvidia shares dropped 14% on Friday after a Reuters report that the SEC is examining the company's accounting.
The stock ended its seventh straight weekly decline, its longest such streak since the 2008 financial crisis.
The slide follows Jensen Huang's move to step down as CEO, and HSBC cut the stock to hold, citing the lack of a permanent succession plan.
items.why: Nvidia is among the largest S&P 500 companies, so its fall weighs heavily on index and Nasdaq results.

items.title: AMD drops more than 13% after Hunterbrook Capital discloses short position
facts: Advanced Micro Devices fell more than 13% on Friday, moving alongside Nvidia.
CNBC ties the AMD drop to Hunterbrook Capital revealing a short position in the stock.
items.why: A second large chip name falling sharply widened the AI-hardware sell-off beyond Nvidia.

items.title: Anthropic slides about 8.5% on its first full trading day after record IPO
facts: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share and raised about $81.3 billion, the largest offering on record, ahead of SpaceX.
Shares fell about 8.5% on Friday, with an intraday low near the $83 offer price.
items.why: The weak debut fed the view that AI-related valuations are being reset.

items.title: Memory stocks Micron and Sandisk fall 12% to 14% as CoreWeave drops almost 11%
facts: Micron and Sandisk lost roughly 12% and 14% in Friday trading, CNBC reported.
CoreWeave tumbled almost 11% in the same session, during the broad AI sell-off.
items.why: Memory and AI-infrastructure names took some of the sharpest losses in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq.

items.title: UnitedHealth rises on TD Cowen upgrade as General Mills gains in defensive rotation
facts: TD Cowen raised UnitedHealth to buy from hold and named it a top pick for 2027, after a drop of about 20% in three sessions over Medicare Advantage rule proposals.
General Mills rose as traders moved into consumer staples; the shares gained 3.8% on our price data.
items.why: Health insurers and staples gained while technology fell, showing money rotating to defensive sectors.

items.title: BILL Holdings agrees to a $6.0 billion take-private led by TPG, with Corpay as minority partner
facts: BILL will be bought for $63.25 a share in cash, valuing it at $6.0 billion, a 31% premium to its 60-day volume-weighted average price through November 16.
Corpay would invest about $1.1 billion for roughly a third of the equity, with an option to buy the rest in 2030; closing is expected in the first half of 2027.
items.why: A large payments-sector buyout shows deal activity continuing as stocks sell off.

items.title: Boston Scientific prices about $7.6 billion of dollar and euro bonds
facts: It priced four tranches of US dollar senior notes totaling $3 billion, with coupons from 5.375% (due 2029) to 5.875% (due 2036).
It also priced €4.25 billion of euro notes through a subsidiary, guaranteed by the parent; both offerings are expected to close December 1.
items.why: A big bond raise by a large medical-device maker reflects what companies pay for debt with yields near 5%.

items.title: Bessent calls Anthropic an 'only in America' story in CNBC interview
facts: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Anthropic had been very cooperative in pre-testing models with the administration.
He said one of Anthropic's seven co-founders plans a large gift to Trump Accounts.
items.why: It shows the administration's stance toward AI firms while the AI trade sells off.

items.title: S&P 500 falls 3.7% into correction; 10-year Treasury yield slips to about 4.99%
facts: The S&P 500 fell 3.7% to 6,910.39. The S&P 500 and Dow ended more than 10% below their records, and the Nasdaq Composite turned negative for 2026.
The 10-year Treasury yield fell about 6 basis points to 4.989%, after it had risen above 5%.
CNBC lists drivers: Nvidia's slide, a break below the 200-day average, inflation worries with oil elevated, and slowing earnings growth.
items.why: A correction in the S&P 500 and a 10-year yield near 5% set the tone for stocks and bonds heading into the week.
